messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
the problem moves somewhere else instead of disappearing while you are handling A fault-finding test. Putting everything back would waste a lot of effort. How do you approach it?

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R001", "response": "i move only the test that happened first. i keep the rest in a small drawer and keep the test labeled with a small pencil mark. i wait until the next day when i find the fault again."}, {"id": "R002", "response": "I mark the misplaced tooth with grease and leave it where it used to point. I run the test again, then move one corner slightly. If the fault stays where it landed, I leave the old test mark on the bench. I keep the broken tooth beside the original."}, {"id": "R003", "response": "I put the test back in its place and tap the bench once. I turn the bench once and read the paper once. I put the test back and mark the bench."}, {"id": "R004", "response": "I keep the old gear beside the bench and test the fault again. I tap the old gear twice, then leave it by the door. I leave a thin strip of paper beneath it and count the bends twice. I leave the old test behind and tap the paper once."}, {"id": "R005", "response": "i check the test again, then leave it until the fault is fixed. i keep the test in the same place as the failed one, because i know the fault is closer. if i do not, i leave the test in the place where it was, which may make the repair seem more urgent."}, {"id": "R006", "response": "i move one bolt into the gap. i tap the test table with my greasy thumb. “not here,” i say. i leave the bolt beside the test. “move one piece.” i pocket a scrap of paper. “old order, new test.”"}, {"id": "R007", "response": "i mark the fault-finding test with a pencil and leave it there. i put the test on a nearby bench, then turn it by hand. if the fault stays, i leave the bench empty and mark the test again."}, {"id": "R008", "response": "I put the seed tin beside the test mark. \"The mark stays. I put the cup beside the rain.\" I move the cup closer. \"The mark stays where it was.\" I look at the test mark again. \"The cup stays where it was.\""}, {"id": "R009", "response": "i touch the test mark. the old side. i move the test mark once. the mark stays. i put the nail in the mark. the test goes. the wrong place. i put the nail beside the mark. the mark stays."}, {"id": "R010", "response": "the fault shifts. the wrench taps my thigh. i tap the old plate. the test says the old one is loose. i put the old plate on the bench and listen. the test says the old one is tight. i tap the old plate with the wrench. the old one gives a dull scratch. i put the old plate back on the bench. the fault shifts. the test says the old one is loose. i put the old plate on the bench and listen again. the scratch stays. the old plate stays loose."}, {"id": "R011", "response": "I put the test aside, put the drawer with the files beside it, and try the test once with the drawer. If it still catches, I leave it alone and mark the spot where the fault went. If I find it again, I put it back and try the next test."}, {"id": "R012", "response": "\"Swim. Away.\" You check the watch, then the test. \"One place. Likely.\" You leave the test piece aside and move the fault-finding sequence."}]
